fields.description: The completion this certifies. One certificate per completion — a second one for the same pass would be two documents making the same claim with different numbers on them.
fields.label: Completion

fields.description: The title as it read on the day this was issued. Snapshotted, never fetched — a course renamed later must not rewrite a certificate somebody is holding.
fields.label: Course Title

fields.description: The exact version that was passed, carried over from the completion. Provenance for the print format, and the anchor a re-issue would be rebuilt from.
fields.label: Course Version

fields.description: Derived from the expiry date and from cancellation — never typed. Revoked is what a cancelled certificate becomes, and it stays visible so the withdrawal is answerable.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The name as printed. Snapshotted for the same reason the title is: people change their names, and the document already in circulation does not.
fields.label: Holder

fields.description: The learner. Named `user` to match Training Assignment / Attempt / Completion — training/permissions.py scopes every learner-owned row on a column of this exact name, so anything else silently loses row-level scoping.
fields.label: Learner

fields.description: For a customer contact, the account they belong to — this is how a client is shown who on their side is certified.
fields.label: Customer

fields.description: Blank means it never expires. Computed from the course's certificate_valid_months at issue and then left alone — shortening the course setting later must not retroactively expire a certificate.
fields.label: Expires On

fields.description: What the public verification page is looked up by. Deliberately not the document name: names are guessable in sequence, so a serial number on a printed certificate would let anybody enumerate everyone else's.
fields.label: Verification Code

fields.description: Which format produced the HTML below. Recorded for provenance only — changing it does not re-render an issued certificate.
fields.label: Print Format

fields.description: The certificate as it was rendered at issue, stored rather than regenerated. Editing the print format next year must never rewrite a document somebody already holds — the same reason the e-sign lifecycle does not use frappe.attach_print. Writable after submit only so the issuing code may render on either side of submit().
fields.label: Certificate HTML
